home.subtitle: First steps in digital twin solutions.

about.subtitle: A platform focused on optimization, load balancing and dynamic relocation of urban waste containers, integrated with technical engineering standards, traffic safety and logistical efficiency applicable to any city.
about.who_we_are_subtitle: Academic origin, applied engineering and urban impact
about.paragraph1: We are an interdisciplinary research and development team from the Faculty of Engineering at the University of Buenos Aires (FIUBA), passionate about transforming urban public services through Digital Twin simulation models.
about.paragraph2: WAIOT FIUBA was born as an answer to a daily and critical challenge in major cities: container fill asymmetry, overflow on public streets, and lack of real-time data to efficiently dimension and place urban sanitation infrastructure.
about.paragraph3: We design technological tools that empower decision-makers, government urban planners, and waste operators to manage public resources based on scientific criteria and real data.

optimization.title: Container Redistribution
optimization.subtitle: Optimization and load balancing across sites according to historical demand and usage.
optimization.max_distance_hint: Maximum distance between donor and receiver sites.
optimization.history_hint: Period to evaluate saturation for each site.
optimization.overload_hint: Minimizes the hours in the critical zone and overflowing, using each site's history. It decides on its own which sites donate and which receive, so it does not use the utilization thresholds.
optimization.overload_mip_hint: Finds the best combination of moves across the whole network and never relays containers: a site either receives or donates, never both. Slower than greedy: from seconds to a couple of minutes.
optimization.move_cost_hint: Overload hours per week a move must save to be made. Higher: fewer moves, only the most helpful ones. With 0, every move that improves anything is made.
optimization.impact_subtitle: Estimated when the plan was generated and measured since it was activated, against the real network
optimization.baseline_active: 🌱 Active baseline What-If distribution (1:1 replica of physical network).
optimization.adjust_params_hint: Adjust the parameters in the side panel and click “Generate Optimization Plan” to relocate containers in the playground.
optimization.moves_subtitle: {{donating}} donor sites donate containers to {{receiving}} saturated sites.
optimization.plan_deactivated: Plan deactivated: the what-if is the real network again.
optimization.deactivate_confirm_desc: Its {{count}} moves stop being shown and the what-if is the real network again. To measure it again, the plan has to be generated again.
optimization.move_impact_desc: Impact and load balancing between sites
optimization.impact_empty_desc: Adjust the parameters and press “Generate Optimization Plan” to see how the network would do with the plan.
optimization.impact_dispersion_caption: of each site's average fill over the history · before → after
optimization.impact_without_with: without the plan → with the plan
optimization.impact_comparison_error: Could not load what was measured since activation: {{error}}
optimization.impact_no_data_caption: Measured as readings arrive with the plan active.

forecast.title: Forecaster Evaluation
forecast.subtitle: Fill projection backtesting to measure error and critical site detection.
forecast.evaluation_in_progress: Evaluation #{{id}} in progress: {{processed}} of {{total}} sites processed.
forecast.evaluation_failed: The evaluation could not be completed.
forecast.site_count_hint: Random sample among sites with measurements across the whole cutoff window.
forecast.horizon_hint: Hours to forecast from each cutoff. Requires later real data.
forecast.critical_threshold_hint: Level whose crossing should be anticipated.
forecast.historical_lookback_hint: Days before each cutoff that the model sees.
forecast.aggregation_hint: Average summarizes the entire site; maximum prioritizes the fullest container.
forecast.cutoff_info: Several past moments of the history are evaluated, comparing what the model projected against the level each site would have had if it were not emptied.
forecast.run_summary_desc: Context used to interpret obtained metrics
forecast.best_predicted_desc: Sites with lowest MAE in the evaluation
forecast.worst_predicted_desc: Priority sites to review data, collections or demand pattern
forecast.site_metrics_desc: Showing up to 50 sites to keep the view lightweight
forecast.mae_detail: Level error against the uncollected level
forecast.cutoff_count_hint: Number of cutoffs to evaluate. More cutoffs, steadier result but slower.
forecast.cutoff_spacing_hint: With 13 each cutoff falls at a different hour of the day.
forecast.min_history_hint: Cutoffs with less history are dropped. If none qualifies, only the latest is evaluated.
forecast.early_hours_hint: Warning up to these hours before the crossing is a hit; earlier, an extra visit.
forecast.late_hours_hint: Warning up to these hours after the crossing is a hit; later, an overflow.
forecast.event_f1_detail: Balance between warning precision and recall
forecast.event_precision_detail: Warnings that reached a real crossing on time
forecast.events_desc: One case per site and cutoff: a hit if it warns on time before the site crosses the threshold without collection. Sites already critical at the cutoff are left out.
forecast.short_history: Short history: no cutoff had the minimum history, so only the latest was evaluated.
forecast.advanced_options_hint: Defaults are the recommended values; change them only to compare setups.
forecast.group_history_desc: Which data the model sees before each cutoff.
forecast.group_cutoffs_desc: Cutoffs go back from the latest measurement minus the horizon, anchored to a fixed grid: the same data gives the same cutoffs. Each site and cutoff is a case.
forecast.group_window_desc: When a warning counts as on time relative to the threshold crossing.
forecast.events_observed_hint: Cases where the site, if nobody emptied it, reached the threshold within the horizon. These are the ones the model had to warn about. Sites already critical at the cutoff are not included.
forecast.critical_at_cutoff_hint: Cases where the site was already at the threshold at the cutoff. They need a pickup regardless of any forecast, so they are left out of the event metrics.
forecast.too_early_hint: The model warned that the site would cross the threshold, but earlier than accepted (by default, more than 3 h before). It would mean an early pickup: counted as a false alarm.
forecast.too_late_hint: The model warned, but past the tolerance (by default, more than 1 h after the crossing). The container would have overflowed before the truck arrived: counted as a missed crossing.
forecast.horizon_f1_hint: The same F1 without requiring the warning to be on time: it only checks whether the model warned and whether the site crossed. If it is much higher than the event F1, the model detects crossings but gets the timing wrong.
forecast.warning_error_hint: Average hours between the model's warning and the moment the site crossed the threshold, whether before or after.
forecast.warning_bias_hint: Which way it errs on average: negative if it tends to warn before the crossing, positive if after.
forecast.rmse_hint: Level error, in percentage points, against the level the site would have had without collection. Like MAE, but large errors weigh more.
